- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.4) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model tends to lag in correcting downward trends; if 3+ consecutive days of falling prices, adjust forecast to reflect 1–2% faster decline than model.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.4–0.8) and price is volatile, model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts near end of period; reduce final 3–5 forecast values by 1–3% to align with observed mean reversion.
